question.problem:
The annual income of an employee in a large company is normally distributed with a mean of $$50\,000$ and a standard deviation of $$15\,000.$ What is the probability that a randomly selected employee's income is more than $$46\,700$ but less than $$56\,150?$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places. *Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$ $\,0.00\,$ $\,0.01\,$ $\,0.02\,$
$\,-0.2\,$ $\,0.4207\,$ $\,0.4168\,$ $\,0.4129\,$
$\,-0.1\,$ $\,0.4602\,$ $\,0.4562\,$ $\,0.4522\,$
$\,0.0\,$ $\,0.5000\,$ $\,0.4960\,$ $\,0.4920\,$
$z$ $\,0.00\,$ $\,0.01\,$ $\,0.02\,$
$\,0.2\,$ $\,0.5793\,$ $\,0.5832\,$ $\,0.5871\,$
$\,0.3\,$ $\,0.6179\,$ $\,0.6217\,$ $\,0.6255\,$
$\,0.4\,$ $\,0.6554\,$ $\,0.6591\,$ $\,0.6628\,$
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the annual income (in dollars) of a randomly selected employee. Then we have $X∼N(50\,000,15\,{000}^{2}).$

We want to find $P(46\,700<X<56\,150).$ First, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(46\,700<X<56\,150) & =P(\frac{46\,700-50\,000}{15\,000}<Z<\frac{56\,150-50\,000}{15\,000}) \\  & =P(-0.22<Z<0.41)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.22<Z<0.41) & =P(Z<0.41)-P(Z\le -0.22) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.41)-P(Z\le -0.22) \\  & =Φ(0.41)-Φ(-0.22)\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we see that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.41) & =0.6591 \\ Φ(-0.22) & =0.4129.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.22<Z<0.41) & =Φ(0.41)-Φ(-0.22) \\  & =0.6591-0.4129 \\  & =0.2462 \\  & ≈0.25\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected employee's income is more than $$46\,700$ but less than $$56\,150$ is approximately $0.25.$
